approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would authorise spending from the Consolidated Revenue Fund to cover the government's everyday running costs for the early part of the 2016-2017 financial year.
The spending would equal roughly 5/12ths of the estimated annual amount for those services, excluding new policy measures.
Extra funding is provided for agencies with high early-year costs, such as the Australian Electoral Commission.
Authorises interim government funding from the start of the financial year.
Allows normal government operations to continue until a full-year appropriation bill is passed.
Provides extra early funding for entities with high upfront expenses.
The Australian Government and its agencies, particularly the Australian Electoral Commission.

The Supply Bill (No. 1) 2016-2017 seeks $35 billion in appropriations for interim government funding from 1 July 2016, covering ordinary annual services until November 2016, with special provision for the Australian Electoral Commission.

The Supply Bill (No. 2) 2016-2017 seeks approval for just over $6 billion in appropriations from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for non-ordinary annual services, including capital works and payments to states, territories, and local governments, to ensure funding continuity from 1 July 2016. It also sets debit limits for the Nation-building Funds, the Building Australia Fund, the Education Investment Fund, and general purpose financial assistance and national partnership payments.

The speaker thanked contributors and stated that Supply Bills No. 1 and 2, and Supply (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No.1), seek appropriations totalling just over $41 billion for the first part of 2016-17, and must be passed to ensure funding from 1 July 2016 for continuity of program and service delivery.
